questions.q: What is the main weakness of fixed-horizon labeling?
options: It ignores everything that happens between now and the horizon, such as a stop-loss that would have triggered early
It can only be used with neural networks
It requires labeled images
It is too computationally expensive to run
questions.explain: Fixed-horizon labeling only looks at the return at a fixed future point, so a path that breached a stop-loss and later recovered can be mislabeled as a win.

questions.q: In the triple-barrier method, what are the three barriers?
options: Training, validation, and test
Profit-take, stop-loss, and time
Open, high, and low price
Bid, ask, and mid price
questions.explain: The triple-barrier method labels an observation by whichever of the profit-take, stop-loss, or time barrier is touched first.

questions.q: Why does the triple-barrier method produce labels that better reflect real trading outcomes than fixed-horizon labeling?
options: It removes the need for a time limit on trades
It labels based on whichever barrier a position would actually have exited on, mirroring how a real position is managed
It only works on daily data
It uses a larger dataset
questions.explain: Because the label is based on the barrier a real trading rule would have exited on first, it reflects an outcome that rule could have actually realized.

Relabeling historical data after a stock split
A second model that decides whether to act on a primary model's directional call, separating 'which way' from 'how confident'

questions.explain: Meta-labeling trains a secondary model to judge whether the primary model's directional signal should be acted on, which can improve precision and sizing.

questions.q: Which book introduced the triple-barrier method and meta-labeling, referenced throughout this course?
options: 'Deep Learning' by Goodfellow, Bengio, and Courville
'Python for Data Analysis'
'The Intelligent Investor'
'Advances in Financial Machine Learning' by Marcos López de Prado
questions.explain: The triple-barrier method and meta-labeling come from Marcos López de Prado's 'Advances in Financial Machine Learning,' a foundational reference for applying ML to finance correctly.
